label: third original token (t=2), for a preferred subset of tokens (e, v, t, m, u, q, k, b, 1, ...)
explanation: Position detector with token preference. About 74% of activation mass is at step t=2, the third original token; it never fires at t=0, 1 or at t>=6 of the original phase. At t=2 it fires on about 45% of sequences, and how often depends on the input token in a graded way: e (~100%), v (95%), t, m, u, q, k (78-87%), b, 1 (76%), 0 (60%), then s, w, j, p (~45-52%), weaker for most others, and essentially never for o, r, l, z. The top activations are e/t/m at t=2 or just after a short prefix. Secondary mass: t=3 (about 11% of mass, including <DEL> at t=3 when L=3, and the token right after an active t=2) and a weak late copy-phase tail (t=11-17, ~11% of mass). It is mostly silent during copy and on the delimiter. The predicate (t=2 and preferred token) gets dev P=0.73, R=0.53. Plain t=2 alone gets R=0.70 and mass recall 0.74 but P=0.45. Magnitude claims beyond token preference were not checked.
